stories.related_coverage: Separates vendor-reported exploit discovery from maintainer validation, deployment controls and independent safety review.
stories.summary: OpenAI introduced BioBasicsBench, 100 wet-lab tasks tested across seven models, 37 settings and 18,500 graded results. GPT-6 Astra at xhigh reached 66.7%, with a reported 95% confidence interval of 60.3–73.1. The benchmark also exposes failures involving controls, image interpretation and experimental context; all results remain publisher-reported.
stories.why_it_matters: Lab teams can use raw protocols, controls and image evidence to test whether agents reason through experimental context. Treat the reported score as a benchmark baseline, then reproduce failure cases before trusting recommendations in live wet-lab work.

stories.summary: METR’s 11-week, high-access study at Anthropic estimates AI-assisted research and development progressed about twice as fast, with an acceleration index of 1.9x and a 95% confidence interval of 1.5–2.8x. The authors also report sensitivity from 1.1–2.9x, substantial redactions and limits tied to authors, tasks and models.
stories.why_it_matters: Leaders can use the estimate to frame a monitored productivity experiment, not a universal forecast. Track one comparable research output over time, preserve human attribution and expose redacted or model-dependent assumptions before changing staffing or schedules.
